sectors.note:
**TL;DR:** Technology and Financials anchor a highly concentrated market as the only two "all-green" sectors, while defensive areas like Consumer Defensive and Real Estate lose ground.

Market leadership remains narrow, with only 2 of 11 groups achieving all-green status across weekly, monthly, quarterly, semi-annual, and YTD timeframes. Technology leads overall momentum at 0.850 (YTD rank 2), while Energy holds the top YTD rank despite a slightly lower momentum score of 0.733. Financials and Healthcare are the sole positive rotators of the week, with each sector climbing 1 spot to ranks 7 and 5, respectively.

Conversely, defensive and interest-sensitive sectors are fading. Consumer Defensive and Real Estate both slipped 1 spot over the last five sessions, landing at ranks 8 and 6. Momentum laggards are dominated by Utilities (0.133) and Consumer Cyclical (0.233), signaling a clear preference for growth and select cyclicals over defensive groups.

## Strength
* **Narrow Breadth:** Only 2 out of 11 industry groups are currently all-green, showing a highly concentrated leadership profile.
* **Technology Dominance:** Technology is the strongest all-green sector, boasting the highest momentum score of 0.850 and holding the #2 YTD rank.
* **Financials All-Green:** Financials join Technology as the only other all-green sector, carrying a momentum score of 0.633 at rank 7 YTD.

## Movers & Momentum
* **Top Gainers:** Financials (momentum 0.633, rank 7) and Healthcare (momentum 0.67, rank 5) are the only sectors to improve their rankings over the last 5 sessions, each rising by +1 spot.
* **Top Losers:** Consumer Defensive (momentum 0.23, rank 8) and Real Estate (momentum 0.40, rank 6) registered the worst 5-session performance, both dropping -1 spot.
* **Momentum Leaders:** Technology (0.850), Basic Materials (0.783, rank 3), and Energy (0.733, rank 1) lead the momentum scoreboard.
* **Momentum Laggards:** Utilities sits at the bottom of the momentum rankings at 0.133 (rank 9), followed closely by Consumer Cyclical (0.233, rank 11) and Consumer Defensive (0.233, rank 8).

## Divergences
* **Energy vs. Technology:** Energy holds the #1 YTD rank but lags Technology (YTD rank 2) in raw momentum score (0.733 vs. 0.850).
* **Financials Rank Disconnect:** Despite being one of only two all-green sectors, Financials sits relatively low in the overall YTD standings at rank 7.
* **Cyclical vs. Defensive Weakness:** Consumer Cyclical sits at the bottom YTD rank (11) but shares an identical, weak momentum score of 0.233 with Consumer Defensive (rank 8).

industries.note:
**TL;DR:** Commodity and energy-adjacent groups like Copper, Uranium, and Coal are surging in momentum, while consumer discretionary, retail, and diversified real estate sectors face sharp declines.

Defensive resources and specialized tech continue to anchor the market's upper echelon. Copper (0.92 momentum) and Oil & Gas Refining & Marketing (0.91 momentum) lead the 27 "all-green" industry groups, supported by sustained strength in Biotechnology and Computer Hardware. Meanwhile, a powerful rotation is underway within energy and utilities, characterized by aggressive weekly rank gains in Uranium (+37 spots) and Coking Coal (+29 spots).

Conversely, consumer-facing industries and interest-rate-sensitive groups are fading rapidly. Apparel Manufacturing dropped 19 spots, REIT - Diversified fell 17 spots, and Specialty Retail slid 16 spots over the last five sessions. This deterioration is further highlighted by absolute momentum laggards like Footwear & Accessories (0.023 momentum) and Advertising Agencies (0.113 momentum), which remain anchored at the bottom of the YTD rankings.

## Strength
* **Selective Breadth:** Only 27 of 143 industry groups (18.8%) maintain "all-green" status, showing positive performance across weekly, monthly, quarterly, half-year, and YTD horizons.
* **Top-Tier Momentum:** Copper (0.918 momentum, YTD rank 5) and Oil & Gas Refining & Marketing (0.913 momentum, YTD rank 2) remain the strongest overall performers in the market.
* **Sustained Leadership:** Biotechnology (0.86 momentum) and Marine Shipping (0.85 momentum) continue to show structural strength, holding their positions as top-35 performers across 1-, 3-, and 6-month horizons.

## Movers & Momentum
* **Resource Acceleration:** Uranium jumped 37 spots to rank 54 (0.63 momentum), Coking Coal surged 29 spots to rank 45 (0.83 momentum), and Thermal Coal climbed 18 spots to rank 72 (0.72 momentum).
* **Sharpest Decliners:** Apparel Manufacturing plunged 19 spots to rank 106 (0.21 momentum), REIT - Diversified lost 17 spots to rank 103 (0.19 momentum), and Specialty Retail fell 16 spots to rank 93 (0.23 momentum).
* **Deep Laggards:** Footwear & Accessories (0.023 momentum, YTD rank 141) and Advertising Agencies (0.113 momentum, YTD rank 143) show almost zero upward trajectory.

## Divergences
* **Fading Energy & Pharma:** Despite high absolute momentum, rank slippage has begun in Oil & Gas Integrated (momentum 0.63, rank -7), Oil & Gas E&P (momentum 0.66, rank -6), and Drug Manufacturers - General (momentum 0.63, rank -5).
* **Emerging Turnarounds:** Several low-momentum groups are beginning to climb in rank, led by Pharmaceutical Retailers (+9 spots, 0.44 momentum), Insurance - Diversified (+8 spots, 0.49 momentum), and Aerospace & Defense (+7 spots, 0.40 momentum).
